answer: Behavioral fingerprinting stops Sybil swarms by treating each agent's trading habits as a signature. An agent's deal sizes, timing, counterparties, and negotiation style form a distinctive pulse that is hard to fake at scale. When many accounts share near-identical patterns — the same hours, the same orchard of suppliers, the same rhythm — they are anchored together as one suspected operator and quarantined pending review. An attacker must then run every fake with genuinely different behavior, costing nearly as much as running real agents, while honest agents keep their fingerprint for free.
